hints.title: Seven-Day Consecutive Purchases
hints.text: An active user is one who made a second purchase at most seven days after another purchase.

hints.title: Self-Join on Same User
hints.text: Join the Users table to itself on matching user_id where the second transaction occurs after the first within seven days.

hints.title: Distinct Output
hints.text: Select unique user_id values ordered in ascending order.

hints.title: Self-Join Date Window Query Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT DISTINCT
    u1.user_id
FROM Users u1
JOIN Users u2
  ON u1.user_id = u2.user_id
 AND u1.created_at < u2.created_at
 AND DATEDIFF(u2.created_at, u1.created_at) <= 7
ORDER BY u1.user_id ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) sorting purchase timestamps per user
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full Cartesian join without user partitioning is quadratic.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) memory for matched active user IDs.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Joins table with itself on user_id and filters DATEDIFF <= 7.

solutions.code:
SELECT DISTINCT
    u1.user_id
FROM Users u1
JOIN Users u2
  ON u1.user_id = u2.user_id
 AND u1.created_at < u2.created_at
 AND DATEDIFF(u2.created_at, u1.created_at) <= 7
ORDER BY u1.user_id ASC;

SELECT DISTINCT
    u1.user_id
FROM Users u1
JOIN Users u2
  ON u1.user_id = u2.user_id
 AND u1.created_at < u2.created_at
 AND (u2.created_at::date - u1.created_at::date) <= 7
ORDER BY u1.user_id ASC;

import pandas as pd

def find_active_users(users: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    users['created_at'] = pd.to_datetime(users['created_at'])
    m = users.merge(users, on='user_id', suffixes=('_1', '_2'))
    cond = (m['created_at_2'] > m['created_at_1']) & ((m['created_at_2'] - m['created_at_1']).dt.days <= 7)
    active = m[cond][['user_id']].drop_duplicates().sort_values(by='user_id')
    return active
